title: Beach Volleyball Tournament Poster
description: A promotional poster for a fictional beach volleyball tournament held in the Town of Shelbyville, designed to capture the energy and excitement of the event at a glance. Every visual element, from the illustrations to the typography, was built entirely in Adobe Illustrator, showcasing a fully vector based approach to the composition.

title: Furrever Pals Puppy Yoga
description: A branding and UI/UX project for a puppy yoga studio designed to address mental health and community connection in Vancouver. The project spans brand identity, visual system design, and service design, creating a cohesive ecosystem where participants experience wellness while supporting animal adoption. Every asset was intentionally designed to communicate warmth, accessibility, and purpose.

title: MyBCIT Page Re-Design
description: A redesign of the MyBCIT student portal aimed at reducing the learning curve for new students. Through research into student pain points and needs, the redesign simplifies core interactions and improves overall usability, while incorporating BCIT's colour palette in a way that feels modern and refreshed, yet still clearly connected to the institution's brand.

title: Boardwalk Boutique App Design
description: An app concept for a skate and streetwear rental shop, built around how people actually browse, book, and shop in one seamless flow. The design supports real time notifications and store location features, making it easy for users to stay updated and find their way to the shop.

title: Bing: The Redesign
description: The redesign of Bing is to create a more user friendly with features that are relavant to users. Along with other talented designers, we were able to enhance the user experience and layout of the search engin, making it less confusing and clutter, which helps users to get to the point right away when navigating.

title: National Geographics Magazine Design
description: A National Geographic magazine cover exploring the space between imagination and reality. The composition was built using a carefully selected set of materials and imagery, layered together to create a cohesive, evocative visual narrative that invites the viewer to look twice.
